Description
Palladium Bullion Coins are made up of precious metal known as palladium (Pt) which has similar properties to make up the platinum group. This rare precious metal is minted by various mints making their investment and commercial coins.
The palladium coins are highly valued because of their rarity and high demand in jewelry, industries, and other areas.
The 1-ounce palladium maple leaf coins are low premium and beautiful coins for investors that want to invest in palladium at low costs and diversify their precious metals portfolio. The coin belongs to the maple leaf family with mintages of less than 70000 pieces each year; they are precious in terms of rarity.
Minted by the Royal Canadian Mint in 2005, the coins have only been struck five times and have fewer than 150000 minted coins.
Compared to the
Gold Maple Leaf Coins
, the palladium maple leafs are scarce. Each of the coins is minted from .9995 palladium and carries the face value of $50 CAD.
Design of Canadian Palladium Maple Leaf:
The 1 oz Canadian Palladium Maple Leafs have the classic design of any other maple leaf coin like other precious metals. The Canadian palladium maple coins are pure bullion coins with .9995 pure platinum.
The obverse features her Majesty, Queen Elizabeth II, along with ‘ELIZABETH II’ inscriptions and a face value of 50 dollars.
The reverse features the Maple Leaf coin and the inscriptions ‘CANADA,’ ‘FINE PALLADIUM,’ ‘1 OZ PALLADIUM’, and ‘9995’ describing its metal content, purity, and mintage.
1 oz Palladium Maple Leaf Coin Highlights:
Contains 1 troy oz of
.9995 pure palladium
.

Royal Canadian Mint
.

Carries the face value of CAD $50.
Backed up by the Canadian Government.
Features her Majesty, Queen Elizabeth II, along with the year minted.
Individual coins come in Plastic Flips Packaging and are package insured.
